summary:
The study you're looking for is Jackson et al., published in *Lasers in Surgery and Medicine* in December 2009 (41(10):799-809, PMID 20014253). It is a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial of a 635 nm multi-diode laser for contouring the waist, hips, and thighs.

- **Design:** The trial ran from May 2007 to June 2008 at multiple private practices in the US and enrolled 67 volunteers aged 18-65 with a BMI of 25-30. The trial was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of a 2-week non-invasive laser treatment. Sixty-seven volunteers between the ages of 18-65 with a body mass index (BMI) between 25 and 30 kg/m(2) and who satisfied the set inclusion criteria participated. Eight participants lacked circumference data at the 2-week follow-up.
- **Follow-up work:** A later six-week protocol study by the same group reported a mean combined circumference reduction of 5.4 inches and no adverse events, concluding that one weekly treatment for six weeks was clinically effective and may be more effective than the previous two-week protocol.
- **Independent check:** A separate 2013 PubMed entry lists an independent evaluation of 635 nm LLLT for waist, hip, and thigh contouring, but I did not retrieve its findings.

I did not retrieve the full text, so I cannot confirm the trial's exact circumference results or its statistical outcomes. The PubMed abstract is the best source for those details.
